findings.element: [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick — src/across.css:169 resets only the base .b-tick to left:0; the lead override at src/timeline.css:710 (left:-24px) and the [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] override at src/timeline.css:1829 (left:-28px) still win
findings.problem: In every across configuration the nearest moment's mark sits 28px LEFT of its own date. On timeline.owner-flight at 1920 the day-16 item box is at x=524.5 and its tick centre is at 496.5 (computed left:-28px); every other tick centre equals its item x to within 0.1px. Reproduces identically at 1920/1440/1280/1024 and at 768 with &layout=across, on paper and on ink. The scale is 20.28px/day at 1920, so the accent reads 1.4 days early; at 768-across the scale is 5.92px/day, so it reads 4.7 days early. The tick also stands 24px clear of the foot of its own leader stem (.b-item::after starts at left:0), so the one filled indigo mark on the measure does not touch the line that claims it. On a surface whose whole thesis is that position is the quantity, the single accented object — the next thing Orla has to do — is the only one that lies, and it is the first thing the eye lands on.
findings.fix: Add to src/across.css immediately after the .b-tick block at 169-173: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; top: var(--rule-y); }`. Six compound units beats both the 4-unit rule at timeline.css:710 and the 5-unit [data-medium] rule at timeline.css:1829, so no !important and no change to the down measure. Then add to interaction-check.mjs: for every .b-item inside a [data-across="true"] measure, assert |tick centre − item left| <= 1px, at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1024.

findings.element: [data-app="notes"] .deskFactLink[data-act="open-task"] and .peelSent + .act[data-act="open-task"] — notes.seam after pressing [data-act="send"]; src/notes.js (desk meta + peel receipt), src/notes.css (.deskFactLink, .peelSent)
findings.problem: At the one moment that justifies the suite existing, the surface answers once-asked four times. Measured at 1440x960 with no scrolling (document scroll 0), after Send to Tasks the string 'Switch on before guests arrive, not when' is printed three times: .deskFactLink at (815,294) 13px/400 under the eyebrow IN TASKS AS, .peelSent at (272,445) 17px/600 under the eyebrow TASKS HAS IT, and a <b> at (264,667) 15px/400 in the ALREADY IN TASKS row. Two eyebrows name one fact two ways. Two separate controls both carry data-act="open-task" to the same destination, 233px apart — .deskFactLink at y=294 (accessible name 'Open in Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when. Your note stays here.') and .act at y=527 ('Open in Tasks'). The reassurance is doubled too: .peelSent's 'Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit.' repeats the meta link's own 'Your note stays here.' Meanwhile the loudest rendering (17px/600) is the transient receipt and the durable record is the 13px/400 one, so prominence runs backwards. The same flow on a phone renders 2 occurrences and 1 control, which is the right shape — the duplication is desk-only, created by the meta column.
findings.fix: While the receipt card is on screen, make it the only site: (a) drop the repeated title line from .peelSent so the receipt reads 'Tasks has it.' + the existing reassurance sentence + [Open in Tasks] [Close]; (b) render .deskFactLink as static text for that window (eyebrow IN TASKS AS + the title, no data-act, not focusable) and restore it to the button it already is when [data-act="close-peel"] fires, so exactly one open-task control is reachable at any time; (c) delete the second reassurance sentence — the meta link's accessible name already carries it. Assert in interaction-check.mjs: after send, the task title appears at most twice in visible text (the durable record and the index row) and exactly one visible [data-act="open-task"] exists.

findings.element: h1.headName in [data-app="notes"] .head, sibling of button.headNext[data-act="scope"] and button[data-act="unscope"] — src/notes.js (head template), src/notes.css (.headName)
findings.problem: Pressing .headNext cuts the index from 14 rows to 3. The index head honestly re-reads to '1 to decide / 3 notes', the scope button's accessible name honestly becomes 'Showing only these notes. Press to see the whole notebook.', and a filled release pill appears. But h1.headName — the one sentence that names what is on the sheet — keeps saying 'All your notes' (15px/400, 72% ink, x=549 at 1920) while 11 of 14 notes are hidden. 384px to its right the release pill reads 'All 14 notes' (data-act="unscope", x=933). So the head shows two near-identical phrases side by side, 'All your notes' and 'All 14 notes', and only the one that is a button is true; the true statement lives in the accessibility tree and not in the visible words. The visible on-state is otherwise a 2px indigo inset rule above the pressed words — a vocabulary Orla has no way to learn. Reproduces at 1280/1440/1920; the phone head does not render the h1 and is unaffected.
findings.fix: In the notes head template, key .headName's text off the scope state instead of hard-coding it: when the scope button is pressed render the scope's own name plus the word that says it is narrowed — 'Mara & Finn only' — and restore 'All your notes' on unscope. That leaves one scope statement, one release control, and no near-homograph pair. Assert in interaction-check.mjs: after pressing [data-act="scope"], .headName's text is not 'All your notes'.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"] .card .cardNote in the board view between 1100 and 1279px — the board/list crossing at 1100 (src/tasks.js) and the tray floor (src/tasks.css .tray min/max width)
findings.problem: There is a 180px-wide band where the board is kept and its cards stop saying what to do. Measured on tasks.dense: at 1280 zero of eight card notes are trimmed; at 1279 all eight are, and at 1100 the notes render 18-45 per cent of their text in 196px lanes. 'Add Northlight (photography) and County Marquee. Drop the lapsed DJ.' renders as 'Add Northlight (photography)…' at every width from 1100 to 1279 — the instruction is the part that is gone. 'Top table moved away from the speakers, check sightlines to the arch.' renders 23 per cent at 1180. At 1100 one card title is trimmed as well. The board's own two automated loops straddle this exactly: five lanes are proved to FIT at 1180, and a note is proved to READ IN FULL only at 1280 and 1440, so nothing checks reading at 1180. The list view that solves it already exists and is switched on 1px lower, at 1099, where the same notes are read whole. Trims are whole-word and the full string is in the accessible name, so this costs a screen-reader user nothing and costs sighted Orla the content of every card.
findings.fix: Raise the board-to-list crossing from 1100 to 1280 — the width at which the board's own card is already proved to work — so 1100-1279 gets the list, where a row is full-sheet width and no note is trimmed. One number, and the list view needs no new work. Then extend the existing note loop in interaction-check.mjs from [1280, 1440] to [1100, 1180, 1279, 1280, 1440] asserting zero trimmed notes in whichever view each width serves, which locks the crossing to the measurement rather than to a round number.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"] .tray[data-lane] .trayBody[data-more] and the .tray::after fold rule — src/tasks.css:812-827, set by measureEdges() at src/tasks.js:3761
findings.problem: In the state built to test density, 10 of 32 tasks are hidden and nothing on the sheet says so in words. At 1920x1000 on tasks.dense the To Do scroller runs 195-775 and its fifth card ends at exactly 775, so no card peeks; '+ Add here' sits at 779, four pixels below the cut, in the position that conventionally terminates a list. Five tasks — 'Price the extra hour on the bar for Nora & Cian', 'Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet', 'Pencil the autumn date in the diary', 'Service the terrace heaters before October', 'Replace the two broken chairs in the barn' — are entirely below it. In Progress hides 2 of 7 and Done 3 of 9. The scrollbar gutter is 0px, there is no mask. The two cues are a 1px rule at rgba(17,17,17,0.08) — the identical --line token every card border is drawn in — and the numeral 10 at 11px/400/62 per cent ink, 630px away at the far right of the lane head, which requires Orla to count the visible cards and subtract. The fold rule was chosen over a gradient for a good rendering reason recorded in the CSS; the gap it leaves is that the cue carries no word.
findings.fix: Give the fold a word. While .trayBody[data-more] is set, render one row at the foot of the tray, above .trayAdd, reading '5 more below' in the same treatment as .trayCount (13px/400, 62 per cent ink), as a button that scrolls its own lane by one clientHeight; derive its number from the same accessor the lane head count uses so the two can never disagree, and remove the row when data-more clears. Keep the hairline. Assert in interaction-check.mjs: on tasks.dense at 1920 and 1440, every lane whose trayBody has data-more shows a visible worded residue whose number equals lane count minus fully-visible cards.

biggestWin: The suite's central claim is not a diagram, it is measured behaviour: I typed an unsent draft into Notes, narrowed the notebook to Mara & Finn, walked the spine to Tasks and on to Timeline and back, and came home to the same 31-character draft still in .topField and the same 3-of-14 filter still pressed — nothing torn down, nothing lost. Underneath it the information discipline is at benchmark level and it is what makes the surface legible without training: every count derives from the rendered data through one accessor (14 notes / 8 to decide / group sums of 1+1+3+2+1; five lane counts summing to the head's 32; the seam decrementing '8 to decide' to '7' and incrementing '3 so far' to '4' in the same paint), time is anchored on every screen that shows a date, the empty lane says 'Nothing held up.' rather than a templated blank, and the whole 13-card board is 18 tab stops with roving inside the cards and inside the rail. That floor is why the five defects above are all local polish and one small decision rather than anything structural.
